summary: The accepted owning-plan addition in .github PR #4541 records a source-only proposal, not an activated publisher or operating grant. The proposed .104 extension uses one mutually exclusive literal profile on the existing publisher, with a trusted closed workflow/artifact-name pairing, exact-source fresh genesis, existing protected journal/admission/16-effect ordering and unchanged historical selections. Journal22 is only a proposal: the accountable authority must allocate and verify an unused identity. Before .104 publisher preflight, credentials or genesis, the root and release authority must authenticate a supported disposition of original .103 effects. Original tag:intent and unknown dispatch outcome remain unresolved; public absence cannot prove non-dispatch. If .103 promotes, the .104 predecessor assumption .102 must refuse and the whole candidate must be requalified. A suspension or supersession would require a separately reviewed installed durable authority/exclusion route; none is established. Candidate source/byte qualification can advance separately under its own admission. The cited executable publisher still selects .103 and its verifier still accepts only the old candidate workflow/name. Changing verifier or feed dependencies does not refresh original .103 compatibility pins. Even publish=false on the credentialed publisher exchanges App/NuGet credentials; source and inert controls do not establish issuance, scope, expiry or effect authority. Publication, both-feed readback and downstream installed acceptance remain distinct.
title: Closed .104 release proposal preserves original .103 uncertainty
